correctness.rationale: For every positive axis triple, the 14 oriented facet normals and 24 square-triangle edges classify every generic projection into 6 or 8 silhouette edges, determined by a strict weighted triangle inequality. A Haar-uniform view separates each pair of edge-adjacent outward normals with probability their angle divided by pi; summation gives the exact Bernoulli parameter. The sharp lower bound follows from unique constrained maximum of sum arcsin sqrt(t_i), and the strict upper endpoint and entire attainable interval follow from boundary values and continuity. The code directly checks original projected hulls and the independent spherical-cone formula. Exceptional directions are null; simulations are supplemental.
